newsitem.title: USA: Tropical storm warnings go up in Caribbean.
newsitem.headline: Tropical storm warnings go up in Caribbean.

text.p: Tropical storm warnings were issued from Martinique through the British Virgin Islands on Saturday as Tropical Storm Hortense approached the islands, the National Hurricane Center said.
At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), Hortense was located about 90 miles (144 km) east of Guadeloupe and Dominica, at latitude 15.7 north and longitude 60.1 west.
The storm was packing winds of about 40 mph (65 kmh) and moving west-northwest at 13 mph (20 kmh).

Hortense gathered strength in the wake of Hurricane Fran, which hit the U.S. coast on Thursday, wreaking havoc through the Carolinas and leaving at least 18 people dead. Hortense was upgraded to tropical storm status at mid-morning on Saturday.

The string of tiny Leeward Islands -- including Martinique, Dominica, Guadeloupe, Antigua, Montserrat, the U.S. Virgin Islands and the British Virgin Islands -- immediately issued tropical storm warnings and urged residents to prepare.
Forecasters said it was too early to predict whether Hortense would threaten the U.S. mainland.
"It's way too early to know if the continental United States is going to be affected. There's so much time that any number of factors could turn it away," said Ed Rappaport of the hurricane center.
In three days, Hortense was expected to be near Haiti and the Dominican Republic, which share the island of Hispaniola. The island is about 700 miles south of Florida.
Tropical storm force winds extended outward up to 60 miles (95 km) east of the center.
Hortense was also dumping rain of up to 10 inches (25 cms) along its path.
